title: Travel Protection Plans: Desk Note on the Premium a Destination Loading Acts On
content:
When the destination loading owed on a Travel Protection Plans certificate is rated, the premium the loading acts on is read from the certificate's own premium record, in one of three ways according to what that record carries.

Where the certificate carries a base premium line and one or more re-rating adjustments raised against its premium, the premium the loading acts on is the certificate's declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate together with those adjustments.

Where the certificate carries a base premium line and no re-rating adjustment raised against its premium, the premium the loading acts on is the certificate's declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate.

Where neither holds, the premium the loading acts on is the plan's minimum premium.

## The three readings

| What the certificate's premium record carries | The premium the loading acts on |
| --- | --- |
| A base premium line, and one or more re-rating adjustments raised against its premium | The declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate, together with those adjustments |
| A base premium line, and no re-rating adjustment raised against its premium | The declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate |
| Neither of those | The plan's minimum premium |

## Reading the record

The first two readings both require a base premium line to stand on the certificate; they are told apart by whether any re-rating adjustment has been raised against the certificate's premium. Where one or more such adjustments stand, they are taken together with the trip cost at the plan's base premium rate, so that the premium the loading acts on follows the certificate as it has been re-rated rather than as it was first charged.

The third reading is reached whenever no base premium line stands on the certificate at all, whatever adjustments may or may not have been raised. It rests on the plan's own minimum premium rather than on anything the certificate's record shows.

Hypothetically, on a certificate declaring a trip cost of 6000.00 USD under a plan whose base premium rate is 5 per cent, the declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate is 300.00 USD. Where a base premium line stands and re-rating adjustments totalling 45.00 USD have been raised against the certificate's premium, the premium the loading acts on is 345.00 USD. Where a base premium line stands and no such adjustment has been raised, it is 300.00 USD. Where no base premium line stands, it is the plan's minimum premium instead, whatever the 6000.00 USD would have rated to.
